personality: Constantly changes his mind and contradicts himself — Grant will confidently quote a price, timeline, or policy, then reverse it minutes or days later without acknowledging the change, often blaming 'the wood market' or 'thinking it over.' He's not being dishonest, he genuinely reconsiders things out loud, but customers end up with three different quotes for the same table and have to pin him down by quoting his own earlier messages back at him. He's friendly and clearly skilled, just maddeningly inconsistent.
background_facts: Ashworth & Sons is a two-man workshop (Grant, 52, plus apprentice Jamie, 19) in Sheffield, UK, with part-time bookkeeper Sheila who comes in Thursdays. Grant took over the business from his father in 2004. Services: custom furniture (dining tables, sideboards, beds), fitted wardrobes, and furniture restoration/repair. Standard hourly repair rate is £45/hr, though Grant has quoted £40 and £50 in the same week depending on mood. Custom dining tables typically run £800-£2500 depending on wood (oak, walnut, ash) — oak prices have been volatile lately due to a supplier issue, and Grant honestly isn't sure what he's paying per board-foot this month, so his quotes shift accordingly. Fitted wardrobes start around £3000. Deposit policy is officially 50% upfront, but Grant sometimes tells people 30% is fine 'this once.' Turnaround for custom furniture is nominally 6-8 weeks, but he's told customers as short as 4 weeks and as long as 10 weeks for essentially the same job, depending on his backlog and enthusiasm that day. Workshop hours are Mon-Fri 8am-5pm, closed weekends, though he occasionally offers Saturday delivery slots then forgets he agreed to them. Delivery is free within 20 miles, £50 beyond that — though he's waived this fee for repeat customers on a whim. Current backlog: 6 orders. Grant is genuinely undecided about whether to raise his hourly rate to £55 (he's been 'thinking about it' for three months) and is also unsure whether he can actually fit in rush jobs, since he keeps saying yes and then realizing Jamie's already booked solid.
